# progress_bar { #labdata.core.progress_bar }

```python
labdata.core.progress_bar(items, description, enabled)
```

Wrap an iterable in a progress bar when one is wanted.

Scanning is one step per repository, so that is what the bar counts.
``tqdm.auto`` is used, which draws a widget in a notebook and a text bar in
a terminal, so the same call suits both.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**items**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} []{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   What is about to be iterated. Its length is the total.

<code>[**description**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Label shown beside the bar.

<code>[**enabled**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Whether to draw one at all. The caller decides: a command line hides it when its output is not a terminal, a notebook always shows it.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} []{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   `items`, wrapped when a bar is wanted and unchanged otherwise. A missing `tqdm` also leaves it unchanged rather than failing.
